analysis_packet.certificate: Construct one independent, online-only cache policy from the task contract. Preserve the required Policy interface, standard-library-only execution, unique integer eviction keys, current-cache validity, and capacity safety. Treat all implementation-specific anchor mechanisms, data structures, thresholds, behavioral choices, and repair lineage as quarantined and non-inheritable. The policy must make its own contract-grounded choices for scan resistance, phase-shift adaptation, object and byte hit rate, and regret, using only observations available through prior accesses and the current request.
exact_actions: Ignore anchor_policy contents and all anchor-derived implementation or repair details.
Translate the task and contract into the obligations and admissibility boundaries above before selecting any mechanism.
Design one fresh policy architecture whose state and decisions are explainable solely from online accesses and current capacity.
Specify safe handling for hits, misses, repeated keys, oversized objects, zero capacity, and all eviction responses.
Check each eviction response against current-cache membership, integer-key uniqueness, and capacity accounting before returning it.
Use behavioral reasoning or local trace examples covering hot reuse, scans, and phase transitions as evidence for the retained commitments.
Pass the producer only this constitution together with the permitted direct task and contract context; withhold implementation details and lineage information.
obligations: Expose exactly __init__(capacity_bytes: int) and access(key: int, size: int, now: int) -> list[int].
Use only Python standard-library facilities and remain deterministic or otherwise contract-safe under online sequential execution.
Maintain an internally coherent representation of the keys the policy believes are currently cached, including byte accounting sufficient to enforce the capacity bound.
Return only keys currently cached by the evaluator, never duplicate a key, and never return the requested key unless it was already cached and is validly evicted under the chosen policy semantics.
Ensure every admitted object fits within capacity after all returned evictions; never exceed capacity_bytes, including empty and oversized-capacity cases.
Use request recency, frequency, size, age, or other signals only as online observations, without assumptions about hidden traces or offline knowledge.
Make admission and eviction choices that explicitly support scan resistance and phase-shift adaptation while balancing object hit rate, byte hit rate, and offline-regret-oriented behavior.
Do not copy, reconstruct, adapt, or semantically preserve any quarantined anchor mechanism or repair lineage.
Emit one complete policy artifact only; do not emit alternatives, rankings, patches, or evaluator-specific logic.
witnesses: Initialization accepts an integer capacity and establishes state whose represented cached bytes never exceed the nonnegative capacity bound.
Every access consumes only key, size, now, and internally accumulated online state; no future trace, score, oracle, benchmark, filesystem, network, subprocess, or external package is consulted.
A hit returns no eviction for that request unless independently required by the contract, and a miss admits an object only when doing so can preserve capacity safety.
Every returned key is an integer, unique within the response, and currently represented as cached immediately before evaluator application of that response.
Across arbitrary request sequences, tracked occupancy after each response is never greater than capacity_bytes.
Oversized objects and zero-capacity cases terminate safely without producing invalid eviction keys.
Behavioral evidence must include both repeated-hot-object accesses and streaming scans, plus a workload phase transition demonstrating adaptation without violating the direct validity obligations.
